title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the table incorrectly says automation for setting a library's default label is not documented; Microsoft describes the REST property that sets it. The roadmap facts and the administrator-created policy route are supported. The checklist also names an auto-labeling policy that is missing from the controls table.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to auto-label existing SharePoint files with their document library's default sensitivity label without manual user labeling.
claims.quote: Enables auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn documents an auto-labeling policy that applies library default labels to eligible existing files at rest.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented existing-files capability requires administrator configuration, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies. ... Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy

claims.claim: The ordinary library-default setting applies its label to newly uploaded files.
claims.quote: Then, any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied

claims.claim: The ordinary library-default setting also applies to existing files when users edit them.
claims.quote: any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied

claims.claim: The library-default page describes application where a file has no label or a lower-priority label.
claims.quote: if they don't already have a sensitivity label, or they have a sensitivity label but with lower priority.

claims.claim: The separate library-default page still lists existing files at rest as a limitation.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The ordinary library-default setting overrides lower-priority labels except manually applied labels.
claims.quote: Default sensitivity label for a document library: Location-based labeling, applicable only for SharePoint. Overrides a lower-priority label unless manually applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Sensitivity-label encryption can change who can open a file.
claims.quote: When a document, email, or meeting invite is encrypted, access to the content is restricted ... Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels to sources to support the statement about encryption restricting who can open a file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The library-default page excludes label encryption configurations with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected. This setting is sometimes referred to as "user-defined permissions".

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label configured with user access expiry other than Never is unsuitable as a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption ... don't support a default sensitivity label ... User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label configured with Double Key Encryption is unsuitable as a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption ... don't support a default sensitivity label ... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Site admin permissions are required to apply or change a document library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Site admin permissions are needed to apply and change the sensitivity label in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Libraries with SharePoint Information Rights Management enabled cannot select a default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: If a library is enabled for IRM, you won't be able to select a default sensitivity label.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Applied sensitivity label file is the documented audit event for library-default labeling.
claims.quote: use the audit log search tool and the Applied sensitivity label file auditing event from the Sensitivity label activities group.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: ActionScourceDetails 6 identifies application by the document library default in the documented library-default audit flow.
claims.quote: identify the value for ActionScourceDetails. ... A value of 6 is used for when the label was applied because of the default sensitivity label for the document library.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly document whether the existing-files policy uses the same audit value.
claims.quote: Searched: '"existing files" "library" "ActionScourceDetails"'; read the library-default monitoring section and the existing-files section of apply-sensitivity-label-automatically. Neither explicitly assigns value 6 to the existing-files policy.

claims.claim: The library-default label tooltip reads This file has been automatically labeled.
claims.quote: the tooltip for the label name displays This file has been automatically labeled.

claims.claim: The same tooltip also appears for auto-labeling policies and users' policy default labels, so it is not unique to library defaults.
claims.quote: this tooltip isn't exclusive to the default sensitivity label for a document library. It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies or as a result of a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn supplies no government-cloud rollout window for the existing-files policy beyond the roadmap target.
claims.quote: Searched: '"default" "library" "existing files" "GCC" sensitivity labels'; searched the fetched auto-labeling page for GCC, government and DoD and read its regional prerequisite and existing-files section. No government-cloud rollout window was found.

claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services

claims.claim: User licensing depends on the features used, with feature-level requirements linked from the Purview service description.
claims.quote: the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use. ... see the Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labeling section and related PDF download for feature-level licensing requirements.

claims.claim: The auto-labeling page says E3 or Business Premium alone does not include auto-labeling of files and emails and requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.claim: No distinct license specific to the existing-files library-default policy is published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"library" "existing files" "license" auto-labeling default labels'; read auto-labeling licensing and existing-files sections and Purview service-description sensitivity-labeling tables. No distinct existing-files SKU was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No meter specific to applying library defaults to existing files is published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"library" "existing files" "license" auto-labeling default labels'; read auto-labeling licensing and existing-files sections, get-started licensing/billing and Purview service-description labeling tables. No meter for this policy type was found.

claims.claim: The library-default page's requirements section does not itself name a license.
claims.quote: Searched: 'license' in sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-default-label; read Requirements in full: label publication, Office integration, PDF support, IRM incompatibility, site admin permissions and nonempty files. No license is named in that section.

claims.claim: The library-default prerequisites include published labels with Files & other data assets scope.
claims.quote: created and published sensitivity labels that include the label scope of Files & other data assets and these labels are published to the users who will select a default sensitivity label

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: You've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: PDF labeling requires adding PDF support in SharePoint.
claims.quote: To support sensitivity labels for PDFs, you've added support for PDFs in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy requires permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy also requires permission to read the site and library metadata needed to identify configured default labels.
claims.quote: You have permission to read the SharePoint site and document library metadata required to identify libraries with default sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to select specific SharePoint sites for this policy.
claims.quote: When you create the policy, select the option to apply default sensitivity labels from SharePoint document libraries to existing files. Select specific SharePoint sites rather than All.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to review simulation results before turning on this policy.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.claim: The SharePoint route is document library > Settings > Library settings > Default sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: In SharePoint, navigate to the document library > Settings > Library settings. ... From the Library settings flyout pane, select Default sensitivity labels, and then select a label from the drop-down box.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for setting a document library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: For the default library label, set the DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary parameter by using REST API on a library.
claims.fix: Replace the absence with a REST API side: kind 'rest', call "POST https://<site-url>/_api/web/lists(guid'<library-guid>')", docs https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/dev/sp-add-ins/working-with-lists-and-list-items-with-rest. Add to the row note: 'Updates the library using X-HTTP-Method: MERGE; the request body sets DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploymentmodels/depmod-secure-by-default-step3 for that property and add both pages to sources. The REST reference documents this list-update operation; the deployment guide documents using that library property for its default label.

claims.claim: Extend protection on download, copy, or move is a different scenario and should not be selected for ordinary library defaults.
claims.quote: don't select the checkbox Extend protection on download, copy, or move. This setting is currently in preview and supports a different labeling scenario.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the tenant-wide library-default disable switch.
claims.quote: Searched: 'DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling SharePoint admin center UI library default labels tenant disable'; read the library-default turn-off section and Set-SPOTenant parameter search result. They document the tenant switch through PowerShell, with no UI route.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true disables the documented tenant-level library-default feature.
claims.quote:
This is a tenant-level setting ... Set-SPOTenant ... DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling ... True ... current SharePoint Online Management Shell:
Set-SpoTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true

claims.claim: The tenant-level switch takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: As with all tenant-level configuration changes for SharePoint, it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.claim: After disabling library defaults, previously configured libraries retain their label selection but it is deactivated.
claims.quote: The label selection for the document library remains but is deactivated so new files won't have the selected sensitivity label applied.

claims.claim: Disabling library defaults does not remove labels previously applied as defaults.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that were applied as a default label aren't removed.

claims.claim: Audit > Search is the documented audit-search route in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -RecordType <ID> is a read-only audit search command.
claims.quote: runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog to search for audit log entries within a specified date range and record type. ... Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate 2023/03/12 -EndDate 2023/03/20 -RecordType <ID>

claims.claim: Updated list is the audit event for changes to the library-default configuration.
claims.quote: To audit the configuration setting for this feature, use the Updated list auditing event from the SharePoint list activities group.

claims.claim: The SharePoint Sensitivity column shows the names of labels applied to files.
claims.quote: Use the SharePoint Sensitivity column to see the names of sensitivity labels applied to files.

claims.claim: The governance checklist names an auto-labeling policy control that has no row in the controls table.
claims.quote: Select specific SharePoint sites and review simulation results before turning on the auto-labeling policy for existing files. / Table rows: library default sensitivity label; tenant-level switch; which files were labelled.
claims.fix: The checklist's step to select sites, review simulation and turn on the existing-files auto-labeling policy has no corresponding control row. This is the missing-table-coverage finding; no additional row is required by this correction.

claims.claim: The existing-files capability is documented as service-side labeling.
claims.quote: Use this configuration when: ... You want service-side labeling for files at rest, instead of relying on users to open or edit each file.
